blocks.explanation:
The equation mixes a trigonometric term with a linear term, so no identity solves it exactly: this is a graphical-solution question.
We need every \(x\) in \([-\pi, \pi]\) where \(y = 3\sin x\) and \(y = \frac{x}{2} + 1\) meet.
Plan: know the shapes, make a table of values, draw both graphs, read the crossings, refine to 2 d.p. and check.
steps:
Given: \(3\sin x = \frac{x}{2} + 1\), \(x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
To find: all \(x\) in the interval that satisfy the equation.
Method: Graphical solution (Section 10.2). Plot \(y = 3\sin x\) and \(y = \frac{x}{2} + 1\) on the same axes; the x-coordinate of every intersection point is a root. To place the crossings we use the difference \(d = 3\sin x - (\frac{x}{2} + 1)\): where \(d\) changes sign, the graphs cross.

Shape of each graph
\(y = 3\sin x\): a sine curve with amplitude 3. It is 0 at \(x = -\pi, 0, \pi\), highest (3) at \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) and lowest (\(-3\)) at \(x = -\frac{\pi}{2}\).
\(y = \frac{x}{2} + 1\): a straight line with slope \(\frac{1}{2}\) and y-intercept 1. It rises from \(-0.57\) at \(x = -\pi\) to \(2.57\) at \(x = \pi\).
Why: Knowing the shapes first tells us roughly where and how often the line can cut the curve.

Draw both graphs and read the intersections
Plot the points, join the sine points by a smooth curve and draw the line (see the figure). The graphs meet near
\[x \approx -2.98,\ 0.41,\ 2.33\]
Why: An intersection point lies on both graphs, so at its x-coordinate \(3\sin x\) and \(\frac{x}{2} + 1\) have the same value.

Refine each reading to 2 decimal places
\(d(-2.985) = +0.025\), \(d(-2.975) = -0.010\)
\(d(0.405) = -0.020\), \(d(0.415) = +0.002\)
\(d(2.325) = +0.024\), \(d(2.335) = -0.002\)
Why: A hand-drawn graph is good to about one decimal place. A sign change of \(d\) between the two half-way values shows that the roots round to \(-2.98\), \(0.41\) and \(2.33\). This is the numerical refinement mentioned in the book's Note.

Check
\(x = -2.98\): \(3\sin x = -0.483\), \(\frac{x}{2} + 1 = -0.490\)
\(x = 0.41\): \(1.196\) and \(1.205\)
\(x = 2.33\): \(2.176\) and \(2.165\)
Why: The two sides agree to about 0.01, as expected for roots rounded to 2 d.p.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = 3 sin x (blue sine curve, from 0 at minus pi down to minus 3, up to 3 and back to 0 at pi) and the straight line y = x/2 + 1 (pink) on the interval from minus pi to pi. They meet at three marked points, at x about minus 2.98, 0.41 and 2.33, with dashed lines dropped to the x-axis.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(x = -2.97\), \(0.41\) and \(2.33\) radians. The first root is \(x = -2.9779\ldots\): \(d(-2.985) = +0.025\) and \(d(-2.975) = -0.010\), so it rounds to \(-2.98\), not \(-2.97\). Correct answer: \(x \approx -2.98,\ 0.41,\ 2.33\) radians.
